prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you mean a full remodel (kitchen/bath/whole house) or a smaller repair (roof, siding, flooring, plumbing, drywall, etc.)? That determines the kind of contractor to hire.

If you want a quick local name list I can look up current businesses online — do you want me to search now? (I can’t browse unless you want me to perform a web lookup for current contractors.)

Meanwhile, here are practical steps and tools so you can find a reliable contractor in Joplin, MO, plus what to check when you vet them:

How to find contractors
- Ask local neighbors, Facebook neighborhood groups, or Nextdoor for recommendations and recent experiences.
- Search Google Maps, Yelp, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), and HomeAdvisor for “remodeling” or the trade you need; sort by reviews and recent projects.
- Check the Better Business Bureau (BBB) for complaints and ratings.
- Contact the Joplin Area Chamber of Commerce for member businesses.
- For specialized trades (electrical, plumbing, HVAC) check Missouri state licensing/registration.

What to ask and verify before hiring
- Are you licensed/registered for this work in Missouri? (Get license number and verify.)
- Do you carry general liability insurance and workers’ comp? Ask for certificates that name you as certificate holder.
- Can you provide 3 recent project references with phone numbers and addresses I can visit?
- Do you handle permits and inspections, or will I? (Good contractors handle permits.)
- What is the timeline, payment schedule, and total written estimate? (Prefer fixed-price proposals rather than open-ended hourly estimates.)
- Who will be on site and subcontracting? How do you handle change orders?

Red flags
- Contractor who demands large cash up front (more than 10–20% for materials).
- No written contract or vague scope of work.
- Poor or no references, or a lot of unresolved BBB complaints.
- High-pressure sales tactics or only wants full payment at start.

What to get in writing
- Detailed scope of work (materials, brands, colors, dimensions).
- Start and completion dates and procedures for delays.
- Total cost, payment schedule, and change order process.
- Warranty on labor and confirmation of manufacturer warranties on materials.
- Proof of insurance and licensing, including subcontractor coverage.
- Lien waiver(s) upon final payment.

Sample phone/inspection script (short)
“Hi, I’m calling about a [kitchen remodel / roof repair / bathroom remodel]. Can you tell me if you’re licensed in Missouri, insured, and available for an on-site estimate? Do you handle permits? Can you provide 3 recent references and a written, itemized estimate?”

If you want, I can:
- Search and shortlist several Joplin-area contractors now and return their contact info and recent reviews.
- Draft a detailed RFP or comparison spreadsheet you can use to evaluate bids.
- Provide a sample contract or checklist to use at final walk-through.

Which would you prefer — I search now, or I prepare an RFP/contract checklist for you? And what type of project is it?
